Mouza Census

Download

Mouza Census

Mouza Census was started in Pakistan during 1971 to provide the sampling frame of rural Mouzas for Agricultural Census 1972. In the very beginning, Mouza Census was just a list of Mouzas prepared by the Revenue Patwari of Provincial Revenue Departments, showing status of Mouzas / Dehs like rural, urban, forest, etc. along with detail of area viz total area, cultivated area, area under human settlements etc. Initially the Mouza Census was conducted only in the settled areas with limited information but with the passage of time, information about the facilities available in the Mouza / Village regarding rural development were also included in the Mouza Census. Nine Mouza Censuses have so far been conducted in Pakistan which include Mouza Census in 1971, 1979, 1983, 1988, 1993, 1998, 2003, 2008, and 2020. The coverage of Mouzas Census was expanded to the unsettled areas since 2003 while scope of the last two Mouza Censuses viz 2008 and 2020, has also been enhanced to all the possible development indicators at community level in the rural areas.

The Mouza Census covers two types of information of rural areas, one is used for sampling purpose and is not published while other relates to the rural statistics particularly the development indicators at Mouza level. The identification, cultivated area, and prevalence of livestock are used for sampling purpose. However, facilities available to the rural farming community in the Mouza and if not available in the Mouza, then its distance from the Mouza, are published. These rural statistics shows number of Mouzas at Tehsil, district, province, and country level having a certain facility. The rural statistics and facilities available within the Mouzas and are at some distance are:

In the World Census of Agriculture (WCA 2020) programme published by the FAO, community level information is also proposed as part of the Agricultural Census. Therefore, PBS has conducted the latest Mouza Census 2020 as part of the 7th Agricultural Census to achieve the two main objectives:

  • To update the sampling frame of rural Mouzas for 7th Agricultural Census.
  • To provide community level rural statistics particularly the rural development indicators to gauge the facilities available to the farming community living in rural areas as per guidelines of the WCA 2020.

The data for Mouza Census is published in the form of number of Mouzas having certain facility in the Mouza and if that facility is not available in the Mouza, then distance of the available facility from that Mouza. The report are published as:

  1. Country Report: showing data at Pakistan and provincial levels showing number of rural populated Mouzas having certain facility. If that facility is not available then the average distance of that facility from the Mouzas not having the facility.
  2. Provincial Reports: reporting data for province, each district within the province, and each Tehsil within a particular district.

  • Gilgit Baltistan
  • Azad State of Jammu and Kashmir

Analytical Framework, Scope, Definitions and Classifications

Definition : Consumer price index (CPI) measures the change over time in the prices of goods and services for consumption by households. The main purpose of the CPI with a base year of 2003 is; is to calculate the inflation rate by measuring the change in the prices of goods and services subject to consumption in the market. For this purpose, all final monetary consumption expenditures of households, foreign visitors and corporate population in the country are taken into account. This concept excludes the production of households for their own consumption from consumption expenditures and the relative rents valid for households.

Classifications: Individual Consumption Classification by Purpose (COICOP) was used in determining the weights and calculating the index, and these expenditures were grouped under 12 main groups and 43 subgroups. 404 items are included in the index.
 
International and regional guidance:  There is no significant difference between Turkey’s methodology and the relevant international and regional standards set out in EUROSTAT.

Scope of data

Source of weights:  Household Budget Survey conducted with approximately 15 000 households (3 years total 45 000) from all socio-economic groups annually, institutional population survey, tourism survey for the expenditures of foreign nationals in Turkey and expenditure and turnover information obtained from administrative records. It is calculated by expanding the National Accounts Household Final Consumption Expenditure data with the change rates.

For seasonal products, a constant weight approach is used.

The period to which the current weights belong is:  December of the year (t-1).
 In the CPI with a base year of 2003 = 100, all final monetary consumption expenditures made for the purpose of consuming goods and services domestically are taken as basis. In the index, prices are compiled from a total of 228 districts, including all 81 provincial centers. Within the scope of CPI, 564 710 prices from 27 411 workplaces are compiled monthly and 5 246 tenants are followed within the scope of the index. The number of workplaces and prices may vary throughout the year depending on the seasonal structure. 

Population coverage:  Population coverage of the index; It is determined as the total population living in Turkey, without any discrimination based on income groups or geographical regions.

Geographic coverage:  All domestic final monetary consumption expenditures of households, foreign visitors and corporate population were taken into account.

FPrice coverage:  The price coverage of the index is determined as purchase prices. Prices are determined as cash payments including taxes, and installment sales or negotiated prices are not taken into account.
